ctx.x: Well, who were you playing with when you moved away from there? Do you remember by any chance?

Yeah, we had a band. The Imperial Band. You were playing with the Imperial? Yeah. Imperial Band. Young Imperial. And who had that band? Well, we had that band that was Simon. My cousin Simon and John. Then we had my cousin Sugar New was playing drum with us. Sugar New, huh? Yeah. What was his last name? Sam Fraser. Oh, Sam? Sam Fraser. Well, I heard of him, but I never heard of Sugar New. Well, that's his nickname. Big name. Yeah. I see. But his right name is Sam Fraser. And who'd you say the trumpet was? The…
Trombone player, you must have had it. Maybe a violin player, too.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: Barbarin, John Marrero, and, uh, Artemis Don's bass.

ctx.x: Well, in that time, you see, that was hard and usually. You see, you get a band, you take a link to a day like on a Sunday, or you catch every

band in town. You see, to have work, you have to have a band, you have to have a band, and you have to have a band. But on the Sundays, you catch them big clubs, they get on out there and they watch for the bands. They get to have their band. They get to have their band. They get to have their band. They get out there and they watch, stand up and watch what band's coming along. The band gets the hot with you on one number, it's carrying your numbers. Well what you do, you go back and what you call the Red Bull,…
What else? He was playing clarinet. Clarinet. True clarinet.
